paras: The threatened lynching of George Williams took place at McRae, Georgia, on the night of August 18, 1905, when a crowd of 75 to 100 men gathered to lynch Williams, a Black prisoner charged with an attempted assault upon a white woman. Sheriff Dowdy had learned of the plan and moved Williams to the jail at Macon, and no violence against him was reported. Papers outside Georgia carried the story as a brief Associated Press item crediting the sheriff with defeating the mob.

Williams, described in the dispatch as "a negro," had been held in the McRae jail for about two weeks before the crowd gathered. He was "charged with an attempted assault upon a white woman"; the reports do not name the woman or give the date or place of the alleged offense.

On the night of August 18, men came into McRae "from different parts of the county" for the purpose of lynching Williams, a crowd estimated at seventy-five to one hundred. Sheriff Dowdy, however, had heard that the attempt would be made that night and had already removed the prisoner to the Macon jail. The dispatch does not say whether the crowd went to the jail, what it did on finding Williams gone, or how it dispersed.
No arrests of members of the crowd were reported, and the coverage does not show whether Williams was later returned to McRae or tried on the charge.

The episode survives in a single Associated Press dispatch datelined McRae, August 19, which ran the next day in at least three papers outside Georgia. The New-York Tribune headlined it "Sheriff Frustrates Mob" with the deck "Hurries Negro to Jail When He Hears of Threat to Lynch," while the Newport News Daily Press used "Sheriff Eluded Mob of Lynchers" on its front page. The Richmond Times Dispatch printed the same text on page 18 under "Mob Frustrated."

Each version framed the story around the sheriff's success, stated the charge against Williams without qualification, and offered no comment on the crowd. No report in a Georgia paper or in the Black press was found in the coverage for August and September 1905.

reader.title: Threatened lynching of George Williams
bases: A crowd gathered at McRae for the stated purpose of lynching a jailed Black prisoner, who was moved before any attack (A1, A2).

A crowd of 75 to 100 men gathered to lynch Williams over an attempted-assault charge, but the sheriff removed him to Macon and no one was killed (A1, A2); it was a threatened lynching, not a completed one.
All three reports carry the same Associated Press dispatch from McRae dated Aug. 19 (A1, A2, A3); no independent local or Black-press account was found.
